title: Minimax Rates for CATE Variance with Rough Nuisances and Heavy-Tailed Outcomes

The contribution beyond the generic quadratic benchmark is the multiresolution reciprocal correction preserving unequal collision dimensions, both heavy thresholds and unselected small means, rather than the balanced lower power or scalar clipping inequalities. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived and informally discharged the full unknown-propensity two-heavy correction and matched log-free smoothness frontier, preserving the fixed n^(-4/11) specialization and proving the n^(-2/3) ceiling. The math referee passed, but the delivered-paper referee graded the specialized fixed-design/public-smoothness point-estimation package subfield below the field floor. Formalization was not attempted; the related_work_incomplete finding remains positioning debt and is not the terminal reason.
tldr: For the one-dimensional original-record class with public uniform covariate law, unknown overlapping propensity, Hölder exponent \(0<\sigma\le1\), and arbitrary conditional \(3/2\)-moment outcome laws, the minimax squared-risk rate for centered CATE variance is \(n^{-\min\{8\sigma/(1+6\sigma),2/3\}}\). The elbow is \(\sigma=1/6\), with no logarithmic loss there or elsewhere. A total data-only cubic reciprocal correction attains this frontier. The contribution is the uniform two-heavy unknown-denominator correction, while the balanced quadratic power and canonical robustification receive donor credit.
gap: Exact CATE-variance inference and robust quadratic-functional estimation are available in different experiments. Their hypotheses do not cover the joint combination of arbitrary conditional \(3/2\) moments, Hölder exponent \(1/16\), unknown propensity and the entire original-record law class.
fill: The deliverable is one evaluated numerical minimax rate, a total publicly tuned estimator, and legal full-outcome testing laws. Conditional collision geometry and tail-bias cancellation are supporting steps; an oracle-only result cannot fill the gap.
